1. What is Gryphmark

Gryphmark is a Markdown viewer and editor for Windows. You format text with buttons — headings, bold, lists, tables, code — and Gryphmark writes the Markdown tags behind the scenes. Every document is shown exactly the way GitHub displays it, in light or dark theme.

It is designed for README.md files, notes, documentation and any .md file you want to read or edit without memorising syntax.

2. Installation

Run Gryphmark-Setup-1.2.1.exe. The installer is available in English and Spanish and does not need administrator rights: it installs for the current user in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Gryphmark.

OptionWhat it does
Desktop shortcutAdds a Gryphmark icon to the desktop.
Open .md files with GryphmarkAdds Gryphmark to Open with for .md / .markdown files, and makes it the handler for those files for the current user.

Requirements: Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, which is already part of Windows 11. The .NET runtime is included; nothing else has to be installed.

Up to version 1.1.1 the program was called Quillforge. If that version is installed, the installer removes it, and Gryphmark copies its settings, recent files and recovery drafts on the first start.

To uninstall: Settings → Apps → Installed apps → Gryphmark → Uninstall. Your settings in %APPDATA%\Gryphmark are kept.

3. The window

PartUse
Menu barFile, Edit, Format, View, Language and Help. All menus are available in English and Spanish.
ToolbarThe formatting buttons (see below). Hidden in GitHub preview, which is read-only.
DocumentThe page itself, laid out with the same column width, fonts and spacing as github.com.
Status barFile path, word count, current mode, and whether there are unsaved changes.

The title bar shows the file name; a ● in front of it means there are unsaved changes.

4. Three ways to see a document

Switch with the three buttons at the right end of the toolbar — Visual · Markdown · GitHub —, the View menu or the shortcuts. Hover over a button to see what it does.

ButtonShortcutWhat you see
Visual
Visual editor		Ctrl+1The formatted document. Type and use the buttons; the Markdown is generated for you.
Markdown
Markdown source		Ctrl+2The raw Markdown on the left and a live preview on the right. For when you want to see or touch the tags.
GitHub
GitHub preview		Ctrl+3Read-only page rendered like GitHub, with syntax highlighting, task lists and clickable links.

6. Files

ActionHow
OpenFile → Open (Ctrl+O), double-click a .md file, or drag a file onto the window.
Recent filesFile → Open recent keeps the last 12 files.
Save / Save asCtrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S. New files are saved as UTF-8 without BOM, the same as GitHub; existing files keep their encoding and line endings.
New / New windowCtrl+N starts an empty document; New window opens a second Gryphmark.
Show in folderOpens Explorer with the file selected.

If you close a document with unsaved changes, Gryphmark asks whether to save them.

Images and links

Relative paths work as on GitHub: ![diagram](img/diagram.png) shows the image stored next to the .md file. In GitHub preview, links to web pages open in your browser, links to other .md files open in Gryphmark, and #heading links jump inside the document.

7. Export and print

Export to HTML saves a single, self-contained HTML page with the GitHub style embedded — ready to e-mail or publish.

Print / PDF (Ctrl+P) prints the GitHub-style page. Choose Save as PDF as the printer to create a PDF.

8. Working tools

FeatureHow it works
Find / ReplaceCtrl+F / Ctrl+H open a bar above the document. F3 and Shift+F3 jump between matches; Esc closes it. Aa matches case.
OutlineCtrl+Shift+O or the first toolbar button shows the headings on the left; click one to jump to it.
Your formatting is keptOnly the lines you change are rewritten when you save: list markers, __bold__, table alignment, line endings (CRLF/LF) and BOM stay as they were.
Changed outsideIf another program modifies the open file, Gryphmark reloads it (or asks first if you have unsaved changes).
Crash recoveryUnsaved work is backed up every 20 seconds. If Gryphmark or Windows stops unexpectedly, the next start offers to recover it.
Spell checkView → Spell check underlines misspelled words (Windows dictionaries).
One window per fileOpening a .md while Gryphmark is running brings the existing window forward instead of starting a second copy. File → New window still opens another one.
UpdatesGryphmark checks once a day for a new version; Help → Check for updates does it on demand.
AboutHelp → About Gryphmark shows the version, author, license and credits. Copy info copies the version details, handy for reporting a problem.
Sample documentA sample that shows every feature in the three views. It opens on the first start and from Help → Sample document, and it is pinned at the top of File → Open recent; right-click it there and choose Hide sample to remove it from that list. It opens as an untitled copy, so the original is never overwritten, and it changes language together with the menus.

GitHub extras

Also rendered exactly like GitHub: alerts (> [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING], [!CAUTION]), ```mermaid diagrams, math ($E=mc^2$ and $$ … $$), footnotes ([^1]) and emoji shortcodes (:rocket:).

9. Language, theme and zoom

Language menu: English or Español. It changes the menus, the toolbar tooltips and dialogs immediately. The first time, Gryphmark follows the Windows language.

View → Dark theme switches between GitHub light and GitHub dark. Zoom with Ctrl++, Ctrl+- and Ctrl+0. Language, theme, mode, zoom and window size are remembered.

11. Technical information

ItemDetail
Version1.2.1
LicenseGNU GPL version 2 only (GPL-2.0-only) — free software, no warranty. Full text: LICENSE.txt in the program folder.
Platform.NET 8 (WPF, self-contained) + Microsoft Edge WebView2
EditorTOAST UI Editor 3.2 (MIT)
GitHub renderingmarked (GitHub Flavored Markdown), highlight.js, github-markdown-css (MIT)
IconGriffin from Martin Schongauer's engraving (c. 1485), The Metropolitan Museum of Art, CC0; quill added.
Settings%APPDATA%\Gryphmark\settings.json
Source codesrc/ in the project folder; build with build.ps1.
The visual editor normalises some details when it writes Markdown (for example, * lists become -). The text and the way GitHub displays it do not change.
